overloadMerges.note: The docs render two syntax lines that differ only in whether a leading '*' is passed (selecting whether 'list' is a name-string vs. a reference-number, and correspondingly Text vs. Integer). That's one semantic overload with an optional literal-symbol discriminator, not two overloads. Also restores itemRef's Operator '*' sentinel meaning.

params.name: asObjectName
params.description: If present, 'list' below is an object name (string) referring to a form representation of the list; if omitted, 'list' is a hierarchical list reference number (ListRef).

params.name: list
params.description: List reference number (if '*' omitted), or name of the list-type form object (if '*' passed).

sentinelValues.meaning: the last item appended to the list (via APPEND TO LIST)
the current item of the list (requires the object-name syntax, since each form representation can have its own current item)

params.name: selector
params.description: One of the documented "Hierarchical Lists" theme constants (e.g. Additional text), or a custom property name.

params.name: value
params.description: Value of the parameter; its concrete type depends on which selector is passed.

interactionNotes.note: The literal symbol '*' means two unrelated things depending on position: leading = 'list is a name, not a ref number'; in itemRef's slot = 'operate on the current item'. Using the itemRef '*' sentinel requires the object-name syntax (leading '*' passed).

_needsReview: value's concrete type (Text/Boolean/Real) is selected by which 'selector' constant is passed, similar to the object_map_equivalent selector-dependency pattern, but the full selector-to-type mapping requires the complete 'Hierarchical Lists' constants table which was truncated in the extracted description; not encoded as an enum_ref here to avoid guessing.
